alex_support: Customer (Acct: ACME) reporting intermittent 502s from EU hosted API for ~20m. They say it only happens when users are on the corporate VPN (split-DNS). Attaching their curl output and a short repro.

alex_support: ```bash
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
*   Trying 54.23.12.34...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example (54.23.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
< HTTP/2 502
< content-type: application/json
< date: Thu, 17 Mar 2026 15:26:11 GMT
< content-length: 68
{
  "error": "upstream_tls_error: handshake timeout"
}
```

alex_support: Customer says when they disconnect VPN the calls succeed immediately.

susan_oncall: assigning to net SRE to check resolver/egress path. @matt_sre can you grab egress traces + resolver hits in eu-west-1 around 15:20-15:30 UTC? Also see if any cert rollout tasks were running.

matt_sre: on it. pulling flow logs now. quick note: we did rotate host certs at 15:22 UTC for a small shard (can confirm which nodes) but rotation completed in <2m and internal health checks passed.

matt_sre: flow logs show a pattern: a subset of connections from the customer's IP block are being NATted through their corporate proxy IPs (198.51.100.45) and our edge sees a TCP open -> client hello that never completes. Resolver lookups from their VPN return a private A record (10.20.3.10) for api.redwood.example (split-DNS), which points clients to their proxy.

matt_sre: quick probe I ran from our EU edge to the resolved IPs:```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.20.3.10:443 -servername api.redwood.example -brief
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:SSL alert number 48
---
no peer certificate
---
```

jen_cs: customer confirms the private A record only exists when VPN is on. They say their corporate proxy does TLS termination for inspection. They didn't realize it breaks our pinning/handshake.

matt_sre: root cause hypothesis: corporate split-DNS + TLS-inspecting proxy causes TLS handshake failures (unknown CA / dropped client hellos) which our gateway surfaces as 502/upstream_tls_error. Cert rotation at 15:22 increased TLS negotiation attempts and exposed the proxy failure window, but the proxy is the underlying cause.

matt_sre: mitigation options: 1) ask customer to add api.redwood.example to their proxy bypass / allowlist (recommended), 2) configure strict SNI/pinning on their client side to avoid termination, or 3) we can offer a dedicated hostname (custom host) that resolves to public IPs only and document bypass steps.

jen_cs: I'll draft an email to the client's infra team with repro steps and the openssl output, and request allowlist/bypass for our domain. I'll include the timeline and recommend they disable TLS inspection for a short window.

alex_support: please add ticket link: SUPPORT-12345 and mark P2. tagging @edge-bot to attach edge traces to the ticket.

edge-bot: attached: /traces/4321123456-edge-trace-15-24.pcap, /logs/edge_euw_15_22.log

susan_oncall: noting follow-up: once customer confirms bypass succeeds we can close. If they cannot change proxy, we should discuss private deployment / dedicated hostnames for that account.

jen_cs: Customer replied: they scheduled a test at 16:10 UTC and confirmed errors stopped when proxy bypass was enabled. They will roll a policy change for the org.

alex_support: closing loop. root cause = split-DNS + corporate TLS-inspecting proxy causing handshake failure surfaced as 502s. Filed mitigation steps in SUPPORT-12345 and sent customer guidance. :white_check_mark:
